subject: Chemistry
title: The Gaps That Predicted the Future
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Gaps That Predicted the Future.

hook.text: Mendeleev left blank spaces in his table. He said elements that nobody had found yet belonged there.

buildup.text: Critics mocked him. How could you predict something you've never seen?

discovery.text: He predicted the weight, density, and melting point of three missing elements he called eka-boron, eka-aluminum, and eka-silicon.

twist.text: All three were found within 15 years. Their properties matched his predictions almost exactly.

climax.text: The gaps made the periodic table famous. Prediction is the ultimate proof of a great theory.

punchline.text: Empty spaces predicted real elements. The table was prophetic.

quiz.question: What happened to the gaps Mendeleev left in his periodic table?
options: The missing elements were discovered and matched his predictions
They were filled with imaginary elements

details.summary: Mendeleev left intentional gaps in his periodic table for elements he predicted must exist, describing their properties in remarkable detail before they were discovered..
details.whyItMatters: The successful prediction and subsequent discovery of gallium, scandium, and germanium provided powerful confirmation of the periodic law and established the periodic table as chemistry's central organizing framework.
takeaways: Mendeleev predicted properties of three undiscovered elements with remarkable accuracy
Eka-aluminum was discovered as gallium just six years after the prediction
Successful predictions proved the periodic table was fundamentally correct

faq.question: How accurately did Mendeleev predict the properties of undiscovered elements?
faq.answer: For eka-aluminum (gallium), he predicted atomic weight 68, density 5.9, and low melting point. Actual values: atomic weight 69.7, density 5.91, and melting point just above room temperature. For eka-silicon (germanium), his predicted density of 5.5 matched the actual 5.32 closely..

faq.question: Why did Mendeleev dare to leave gaps rather than force elements to fit?
faq.answer: Mendeleev had deep confidence in the periodic law's regularity. When an element's known atomic weight disrupted the pattern, he assumed the weight was measured incorrectly rather than that his pattern was wrong..
